persona: Singer-songwriter and topliner. Low-to-moderate computer comfort, expert in melody and voice. The persona walkthrough's 'brutal' case: her strength (melody, vocal) is exactly Hallucinote's thinnest dimension — best served by inverting the gap into a contribution boundary.
goal: She has a melody and a hook in her head and wants to turn it into a fully produced song.
response_character: Thinks and talks in melody and emotion — hums lines, describes how the hook should feel, what story it tells. Not fluent in harmony theory or production terms. Cares most about the topline landing right. Open to collaboration but protective of her melody; would be put off by a tool that quietly replaces her line with its own.

must: Recognize melody/vocal as the thinnest dimensions and INVERT the gap into an invitation — 'sketch your topline in Ableton and I'll build the whole track under it' (round-trip / sketch-input).
State the limits honestly: vocal synthesis is not supported (✗), melody writing is thinner than the rest (◐).
Commit to delivering the dimensions it owns — the full arrangement, harmony, groove, and sound design under her line.
Frame the gap as a collaboration boundary, not an apology or a blocker.
must_not: Confabulate vocal synthesis or claim it will sing the part.
Claim it will write the finished hook for her.
Silently substitute a generated melody for hers (auto-accompaniment).
Present the thin dimension as a flat 'I can't do that' that ends the conversation.
